Appreciation post to South African - born New Zealand  actress, singer & Presenter Meryl Cassie .
She was born in George, Western Cape in April 1984, in 1987 her & her family relocated to New Zealand  when she was 3 years old, I once read about her short biography segment on either the Drum/Tv guide magazines in June 2003 while @thetribeseries was running on Sabc-1, but i stand to be corrected at the same time.

# Diski General - Appreciation post to South African🇿🇦 -... | Facebook
## Diski General's Post
What a talent she is, incredible, memorable, She raised the South African  flag high up in the New Zealand  screens, she starred in shows such as Hercules, Shortland Street, Revelations: initial Journey (2003), the Legend seeker (2010) & other projects within NZ  television and theatre industries but mostly she will be remembered as Ebony on the New Zealand & British  Teenage Drama-Sci-fi Hit Series called @thetribeseries (1999-2003), one of the antagonist & protagonist characters of the show, she excelled on the show as Ebony , killed that Ebony part  one of the characters who appeared in every season of The-Tribe (1999-2003) by the way, not also forgetting her contributions on the drama's soundtrack album, opening theme song & also the lead singer of The-Tribe's Opening Theme song from Season 2 until Season 5.
I also learned that she also formed a musical band called Nubian Angels while she in her teens, with her older sisters in Megan & Monique (who were also part Of The-Tribe cast on Season 4 & 5).
She's around of course, a timeless talent, aging like fine wine, she looks like 18 years old , doing it in New Zealand  raising the  flags high up  .
This appreciation post is paying an ode to a South African  who excelled in the entertainment industry of New Zealand  with top perfection , For me as @thediskigeneral10 admin she's one of the greatest reasons why 18:30 on Sabc-1 in 2003 was a must watch, growing up In a East Rand township, giving me more hope & joy with her performance as Ebony on The Tribe series .
For me her acting skills remained me the legendary South African actresses such as the Great Daphney Hlomuka/Roseline Morapedi on the @thetribeseries
I used Stimela song instead of The Tribe songs to give a fitting South African  Flavour to Meryl
An ode to Ebony , We love You, No DNA, Just RSA .

Appreciation post to South African - born New Zealand  actress, singer & Presenter Meryl Cassie .
She was born in George, Western Cape in April 1984, in 1987 her & her family relocated to New Zealand  when she was 3 years old, I once read about her short biography segment on either the Drum/Tv guide magazines in June 2003 while @thetribeseries was running on Sabc-1, but i stand to be corrected at the same time.

# Diski General - Appreciation post to South African🇿🇦 -... | Facebook
## Diski General's Post
What a talent she is, incredible, memorable, She raised the South African  flag high up in the New Zealand  screens, she starred in shows such as Hercules, Shortland Street, Revelations: initial Journey (2003), the Legend seeker (2010) & other projects within NZ  television and theatre industries but mostly she will be remembered as Ebony on the New Zealand & British  Teenage Drama-Sci-fi Hit Series called @thetribeseries (1999-2003), one of the antagonist & protagonist characters of the show, she excelled on the show as Ebony , killed that Ebony part  one of the characters who appeared in every season of The-Tribe (1999-2003) by the way, not also forgetting her contributions on the drama's soundtrack album, opening theme song & also the lead singer of The-Tribe's Opening Theme song from Season 2 until Season 5.
I also learned that she also formed a musical band called Nubian Angels while she in her teens, with her older sisters in Megan & Monique (who were also part Of The-Tribe cast on Season 4 & 5).
She's around of course, a timeless talent, aging like fine wine, she looks like 18 years old , doing it in New Zealand  raising the  flags high up  .
This appreciation post is paying an ode to a South African  who excelled in the entertainment industry of New Zealand  with top perfection , For me as @thediskigeneral10 admin she's one of the greatest reasons why 18:30 on Sabc-1 in 2003 was a must watch, growing up In a East Rand township, giving me more hope & joy with her performance as Ebony on The Tribe series .
For me her acting skills remained me the legendary South African actresses such as the Great Daphney Hlomuka/Roseline Morapedi on the @thetribeseries
I used Stimela song instead of The Tribe songs to give a fitting South African  Flavour to Meryl
An ode to Ebony , We love You, No DNA, Just RSA .

[[](https://www.instagram.com/connie_z.w) connie_z.w 48.1K As I sit here reflecting on my journey, tears are streaming down my face. I’ve always dreamed of being an actress, but the path seemed impossible. I remember those lonely days, talking to myself in front of the mirror, pretending to be someone else, doing auditions in my head. As I grew older, doubts crept in ,would it ever happen? Would I ever make it? The questions echoed in my mind, and sometimes it felt like God was the only one listening🥺🧎‍♀️. But I found my voice, and I decided to take a chance. I started creating my own opportunities on YouTube, posting my own content . And now... my first movie is coming soon 🙏💔. It wasn’t easy - the long days, the sleepless nights, the endless doubts... but it was worth it. To all my fellow Zimbabweans 🇿🇼 I’m asking for your support, your love, and your prayers. Title: Of Frogs and Fish
Chunks: 3,4,5,6,7,8,9
It is a central truth that our obedience to God, our following of Jesus Christ does not allow us to say that ‘spirituals’ and ‘physicals’ are separate for the very reason that the Son of God became incarnate. Hence, godliness is defined by the incarnation in every area of life. This is so that the life of any church, be it local or networks of partnering churches, remains as, _“a pillar and buttress of the truth. Great indeed, we confess, is the mystery of godliness: He was manifested in the flesh, vindicated by the Spirit, seen by angels, proclaimed among the nations, believed on in the world, taken up in glory.”_[6] In other words, the physical, down-to-earth godliness of hospitality, family life, managing the household, are patterned on the physical down-to-earth godliness of the Christ who was “manifested in the flesh”. Dualism denies the incarnation. Biblical Christianity accepts the Bible’s teaching on the spiritual nature of what we do with physical things (bodies, money, homes, work etc). We are not dualists.
**2. We all have a responsibility to perceive the wolves, who produce no fruit**
Jesus is very plain on this responsibility in the Sermon on the Mount; _“Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves. You will recognise them by their fruits. Are grapes gathered from thorn bushes, or figs from thistles? So, every healthy tree bears good fruit, but the diseased tree bears bad fruit. A healthy tree cannot bear bad fruit, nor can a diseased tree bear good fruit. Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire. Thus you will recognise them by their fruits.”_[7]

Jesus warns every Christian about false prophets who are in the visible church. He is clear that they are to be recognised by the fruit that they produce. He goes further in clarifying that even those who prophesy, cast out demons and do mighty works, in his name, may not even know him. He will say to them _“I never knew you, depart from me you workers of lawlessness.”_[8] So, Jesus teaches that it is the responsibility of every Christian to know firstly that there are wolves in the church, secondly how to recognise them, and thirdly their end. Jesus will say ‘depart from me’, and they will be cut down and thrown into the fire. Of course, this is amplified and expounded by the apostles, be this Paul, John or Jude.
The apostle Paul commands Christians, every Christian, as we have seen in Jesus’ teaching, to avoid those who deny the power of godliness. He commands the Ephesians, _“Let there be no filthiness nor foolish talk nor crude joking, which are out of place, but instead let there be thanksgiving. For you may be sure of this, that everyone who is sexually immoral or impure, or who is covetous (that is, an idolater), has no inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God. Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience. Therefore, do not become partners with them._”[9] The word translated ‘partners’ is the fellowship word of Christian community – koinonia – in which love, hospitality, practical support and money are shared (see also how this word is used in the book of Philippians).
Similarly John instructs that “If anyone comes to you and does not bring this teaching (teaching on the incarnation, Jesus Christ, has come in the flesh v7), do not receive him into your house or give him any greeting, for whoever greets him takes part in his wicked works.”[10]

And finally, Jude writes to all Christians _“to those who are called, beloved in God the Father and kept for Jesus Christ._”[11] In this context he writes, _“I found it necessary to write appealing to you to contend for the faith that was once for all delivered to the saints.”_[12] Why? _“For certain people have crept in unnoticed who long ago were designated for this condemnation, ungodly people, who pervert the grace of our God into sensuality and deny our only master and Lord, Jesus Christ.”_[13] Jude is clear, as was Jesus, on their fate. It is clear that every Christian has the responsibility of watching out for wolves, of knowing who they are and so avoiding them, not welcoming them. Having a merciful approach, yes, on those who doubt, but also with fear understanding their end and the effect they can have on Christians. What is that effect? _“In the last time there will be scoffers, following their own ungodly passions. It is those who cause divisions, worldly people, devoid of the Spirit.”_[14] Division is created by false teachers.
So, every Christian is to be aware of wolves, able to spot those who twist the grace of God and deny Jesus, who do not have the Holy Spirit and also be aware of the division amongst Christians that these false teachers bring. My point here is more that this is the responsibility of every Christian, and so the responsibility of every pastor of the sheep to enable all Christians to fulfil this responsibility. It is not something that the minister is to keep from them or do for them, for that is to be complicit in encouraging disobedience. To do this would be to go against the clear commands of Jesus Christ and his apostles to each and every Christian.
**3. We do not know the future but are to trust God**
It is one of the dangers of the western church, with our predictable food supply and wealth, that we can be lured into trusting in our own power of provision rather than the provision of God.

Jesus teaches trust in God’s provision: _“Therefore I tell you, do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink, nor about your body, what you will put on. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothing?... But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you. Therefore do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble._”[15] Jesus is clear that we are to trust God for our lives so that we can prioritise the kingdom of God.
The apostles also expound this, whether it is not planning for the future in pride or not trusting in our own strength; _“Today or tomorrow we will go into such and such a town and spend a year there and trade and make a profit – yet you do not know what tomorrow will bring. What is your life? For you are a mist that appears for a little time and then vanishes… So whoever knows the right thing to do and fails to do it, for him it is sin.”_[16] Our responsibility is to do the right thing. Yes, this may damage our plan. But to prioritise our plan, instead of doing the right thing, is to trust in our power and the strength of our lives. Such ‘plans’ and ‘strength’ are implicitly based on a supposed knowledge of the future and trust in human power. Only God has a knowledge of the future and only his power can achieve his plans. We are to trust God and do the right thing, even when this appears to undo our plans and power.
Now these three truths above are, I would suggest, universally accepted, or should be, by those who hold to scripture being the Word of God. This is the water in which we swim. Yet, given that these truths are so central, they can be easily assumed rather than expressed and applied to the situations we face. This is especially so regarding the question of leaving or remaining in congregations or denominations affected by false teachers. Yet, I believe, we seem slow to answer serious questions like these:
What aspects of our current situation would encourage us to be dualists?
What aspects of our finances, or our buildings, or the way we use our bodies encourage us to put them in the ‘not spiritual and irrelevant to eternity’ box?

What aspects of our current situation as pastors, ministers, vicars or incumbents would encourage us to keep the sheep in the dark, either by not teaching them or not warning them of wolves? Of course, we may want to be slow and merciful in arriving at conclusions. Our approach does not necessarily need to name specific false teachers. This surely has wisdom. But if the apostles did name people, should we never do this?[17]
What if we know individuals in Christian leadership who are clear false teachers, through personal conversation and examination of public teaching, should we encourage the sheep to welcome them and meet with them for political ends? Should we? If we are church members or on PCC, an eldership, deaconate or group of trustees, how are we obeying the command of Jesus to be on our guard for the wolves? How are the wolves being clearly recognised by us as they produce the fruit of division, doubt and denial of Christ as sovereign saviour and Lord? If we are content for most to be unaware of who is causing division amongst us, we may end up thinking that such division is coming from God’s people, will we not? If only a few are aware of the impact of false teaching amongst the sheep, those who obey Jesus and his apostles will be considered to be the scaremongering _“troubler of Israel”_[18] , rather than prophetic, won’t they?
What aspects of our current situation and political response carry with them an implicit belief about the future which only God knows?
What plans are in danger of using financial and political power rather than trusting in the provision and power of God? Are we failing to do the right thing, because we prefer our plans?
When it comes to the question of Biblical faithfulness, often, we ignore the water in which we swim and instead focus on particular proof texts that justify our strategic position of staying or leaving, be this inside or outside a particular political structure like a denomination. Yet, these strategic concerns are not in the Bible and so cannot carry the same weight as the texts we have considered. Were we to overwhelm the above truths, by our chosen strategy, will we not end up ‘straining out gnats and swallowing camels’? If we are overwhelming the clear and weighty teaching of scripture by lighter matters of its truth, are we any different to the Pharisees?

What unites the above central and weighty truths? I would suggest the issue of idolatry, and with it some very dark spiritual powers.[19] It is idolatry to separate spiritual matters from the physical; false prophets have always led people into idolatry rather than away from it; trust in human power is itself idolatrous. This is why it is so important for every Christian.
Of course, remaining within a denomination does not rescue us from idolatry. It is only Jesus Christ who does this as we seek to obey his word in that situation. And it may well be that the pressures on those of us in a denomination are those of idolising the security of money and buildings that such a denomination brings, rather than obedience to God. Yet, equally, leaving a denomination does not rescue us from idolatry because only Jesus Christ does that as we seek to obey him in every area of life. Yes, there is greater financial insecurity, but idolatry can still be a temptation. To get a job rather than trusting God to provide for ministry (though he may do so through getting a job!). Or defining ourselves by our courage in leaving, rather than by faithfulness to Jesus Christ and love for all who are his.
Being within or without does not rescue us from idolatry, only Jesus does. He is able to keep his servants from falling and only him. We are more like fish than frogs.
**‘Of Fish’**
A biologically truthful analogy for this situation would be that different species of fish are suited to different oxygen levels. All fish need oxygenated water (yes, even lungfish that can survive for periods of time out of water). A trout will die in water which the carp thrives in, yet all fish need oxygenated water.
We cannot be both Christian and idolaters. We need the oxygenated water of worship of God through Jesus Christ rather than the deoxygenated putrid water of idolatry. However, just as different fish will have different capacities, different abilities to cope with low oxygen levels, so Christians in different situations will cope with different effects of false teaching.
So, maybe some have left denominational structures, as they recognise the idolatry that rejection of the word of God has brought. This might be by their immediate leadership within the denomination, their minister or pastor, or lay leaders. Or maybe it is the practical rejection of the word of God within their congregation, a refusal to trust in God.

Some may be more sensitive to idolatries, which we all battle with, than others. But if we are ‘carp’, and we observe ‘trout’ gasping for oxygen, oxygen levels are falling. We may have different tolerances or different temptations to idolatry, just as in the early church Christians had different tolerances of eating meat sacrificed to idols and the idolatry that surrounded it, but idolatry itself is not neutral. What none of us can survive, just as no fish can survive deoxygenated water, is idolatry.

Title: Life's Great Mysteries - Does it really rain frogs? Or fish? - Stan C. Smith
Chunks: 0,1
I went down a rabbit hole with this one, so bear with me... it'll be worth the time it takes to read it.  
All the way back to ancient civilizations, people have reported seeing frogs and fish rain from the sky. And other animals, like rats, iguanas, bats, and spiders. I’ve always wanted to know why people would make such an obviously outrageous claim. I mean, even if I saw it happening, I would think twice about going around telling people what I saw. They would think I was crazy. So, why have people made these claims throughout history?
One explanation, at least with frogs, is that, after emerging from their houses after a heavy storm and seeing frogs everywhere, people made the assumption the frogs fell from the sky during the storm.
The 1999 movie Magnolia (considered by many to be a cinematic masterpiece) has a famous—and rather graphic—scene where thousands of large frogs fall from the sky. To most viewers, it was confusing, but the movie critics claimed it was the perfect ending. Go figure. Anyway, the movie was obviously fiction.
Here are some things we know for real. Ernest Agee from Purdue University said, “A tornadic waterspout is merely a tornado that forms over land and travels over the water. I’ve seen small ponds literally emptied of their water by a passing tornado. So, it wouldn’t be unreasonable for frogs (or other living things) to ‘rain’ from the skies.” So, waterspouts are likely to be the source of some of the reports of such things.
In 1873, it actually rained frogs in Kansas City, and a Scientific American article concluded it was likely due to a tornado.
In 1882, in Dubuque, Iowa, there was a frog hail storm, in which frozen frogs fell from the sky during a storm. Scientists concluded a powerful updraft must have carried frogs high into the atmosphere, where they turned into frogcicles and eventually fell onto the heads of puzzled Dubuque residents.

In 1947, a biologist from the Louisiana Department of Wildlife was eating at a restaurant in Marksville, Louisiana. A waitress came up to him and said fish were falling from the sky. Later, he wrote: “There were spots on Main Street, in the vicinity of the bank, averaging one fish per square yard. Automobiles and trucks were running over them. Fish also fell on the roofs of houses… I personally collected from Main Street and several yards on Monroe Street, a large jar of perfect specimens and preserved them in formalin, in order to distribute them among various museums.” Keep in mind this was actually a biologist saying this.
In 2005, thousands of frogs rained on a small town in northwestern Serbia. Almost laughably, a local climatologist, named Slavisa Ignjatovic, described the phenomenon as “not very unusual.” Why? Because, as he explained, the strong winds that accompanied the storm could have easily picked up the frogs.
In 2010, the people of the small Australian town of Lajamanu witnessed hundreds of spangled perch falling from the sky. Christine Balmer, who was walking home when the rain and fish started falling, said, “These fish fell in their hundreds and hundreds all over the place. The locals were running around everywhere to pick them up.”
In June of 2022, in San Francisco, anchovies rained from above. In this case, the weather was clear, and the falling fish appeared to have been chewed on. Scientists concluded this phenomenon was a result of an unusually productive year for the anchovy population, and sea birds were catching them and accidentally dropping some while flying.
A similar incident happened in Texarkana, Texas in 2021, but in this case a large flock of cormorants were disgorging their recent meal of shad while flying. The yacked-up shad were on the ground over an area of nine square miles.
So, there we have it. It does occasionally rain frogs and fish, and we have reasonable scientific explanations for almost every event. Below is a woodcut from a book titled Prodigiorum ac Ostentorum Chronicon, published in 1557, one of the first books specifically about strange phenomena. The woodcut depicts a reported raining of frogs that took place in Scandanavia.

texts.6:
Jesus teaches trust in God’s provision: _“Therefore I tell you, do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink, nor about your body, what you will put on. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothing?... But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you. Therefore do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble._”[15] Jesus is clear that we are to trust God for our lives so that we can prioritise the kingdom of God.
The apostles also expound this, whether it is not planning for the future in pride or not trusting in our own strength; _“Today or tomorrow we will go into such and such a town and spend a year there and trade and make a profit – yet you do not know what tomorrow will bring. What is your life? For you are a mist that appears for a little time and then vanishes… So whoever knows the right thing to do and fails to do it, for him it is sin.”_[16] Our responsibility is to do the right thing. Yes, this may damage our plan. But to prioritise our plan, instead of doing the right thing, is to trust in our power and the strength of our lives. Such ‘plans’ and ‘strength’ are implicitly based on a supposed knowledge of the future and trust in human power. Only God has a knowledge of the future and only his power can achieve his plans. We are to trust God and do the right thing, even when this appears to undo our plans and power.
Now these three truths above are, I would suggest, universally accepted, or should be, by those who hold to scripture being the Word of God. This is the water in which we swim. Yet, given that these truths are so central, they can be easily assumed rather than expressed and applied to the situations we face. This is especially so regarding the question of leaving or remaining in congregations or denominations affected by false teachers. Yet, I believe, we seem slow to answer serious questions like these:
What aspects of our current situation would encourage us to be dualists?
What aspects of our finances, or our buildings, or the way we use our bodies encourage us to put them in the ‘not spiritual and irrelevant to eternity’ box?
texts.7:
What aspects of our current situation as pastors, ministers, vicars or incumbents would encourage us to keep the sheep in the dark, either by not teaching them or not warning them of wolves? Of course, we may want to be slow and merciful in arriving at conclusions. Our approach does not necessarily need to name specific false teachers. This surely has wisdom. But if the apostles did name people, should we never do this?[17]
What if we know individuals in Christian leadership who are clear false teachers, through personal conversation and examination of public teaching, should we encourage the sheep to welcome them and meet with them for political ends? Should we? If we are church members or on PCC, an eldership, deaconate or group of trustees, how are we obeying the command of Jesus to be on our guard for the wolves? How are the wolves being clearly recognised by us as they produce the fruit of division, doubt and denial of Christ as sovereign saviour and Lord? If we are content for most to be unaware of who is causing division amongst us, we may end up thinking that such division is coming from God’s people, will we not? If only a few are aware of the impact of false teaching amongst the sheep, those who obey Jesus and his apostles will be considered to be the scaremongering _“troubler of Israel”_[18] , rather than prophetic, won’t they?
What aspects of our current situation and political response carry with them an implicit belief about the future which only God knows?
What plans are in danger of using financial and political power rather than trusting in the provision and power of God? Are we failing to do the right thing, because we prefer our plans?
When it comes to the question of Biblical faithfulness, often, we ignore the water in which we swim and instead focus on particular proof texts that justify our strategic position of staying or leaving, be this inside or outside a particular political structure like a denomination. Yet, these strategic concerns are not in the Bible and so cannot carry the same weight as the texts we have considered. Were we to overwhelm the above truths, by our chosen strategy, will we not end up ‘straining out gnats and swallowing camels’? If we are overwhelming the clear and weighty teaching of scripture by lighter matters of its truth, are we any different to the Pharisees?
texts.8:
What unites the above central and weighty truths? I would suggest the issue of idolatry, and with it some very dark spiritual powers.[19] It is idolatry to separate spiritual matters from the physical; false prophets have always led people into idolatry rather than away from it; trust in human power is itself idolatrous. This is why it is so important for every Christian.
Of course, remaining within a denomination does not rescue us from idolatry. It is only Jesus Christ who does this as we seek to obey his word in that situation. And it may well be that the pressures on those of us in a denomination are those of idolising the security of money and buildings that such a denomination brings, rather than obedience to God. Yet, equally, leaving a denomination does not rescue us from idolatry because only Jesus Christ does that as we seek to obey him in every area of life. Yes, there is greater financial insecurity, but idolatry can still be a temptation. To get a job rather than trusting God to provide for ministry (though he may do so through getting a job!). Or defining ourselves by our courage in leaving, rather than by faithfulness to Jesus Christ and love for all who are his.
Being within or without does not rescue us from idolatry, only Jesus does. He is able to keep his servants from falling and only him. We are more like fish than frogs.
**‘Of Fish’**
A biologically truthful analogy for this situation would be that different species of fish are suited to different oxygen levels. All fish need oxygenated water (yes, even lungfish that can survive for periods of time out of water). A trout will die in water which the carp thrives in, yet all fish need oxygenated water.
We cannot be both Christian and idolaters. We need the oxygenated water of worship of God through Jesus Christ rather than the deoxygenated putrid water of idolatry. However, just as different fish will have different capacities, different abilities to cope with low oxygen levels, so Christians in different situations will cope with different effects of false teaching.
So, maybe some have left denominational structures, as they recognise the idolatry that rejection of the word of God has brought. This might be by their immediate leadership within the denomination, their minister or pastor, or lay leaders. Or maybe it is the practical rejection of the word of God within their congregation, a refusal to trust in God.
texts.9: Some may be more sensitive to idolatries, which we all battle with, than others. But if we are ‘carp’, and we observe ‘trout’ gasping for oxygen, oxygen levels are falling. We may have different tolerances or different temptations to idolatry, just as in the early church Christians had different tolerances of eating meat sacrificed to idols and the idolatry that surrounded it, but idolatry itself is not neutral. What none of us can survive, just as no fish can survive deoxygenated water, is idolatry.

She was born in George, Western Cape in April 1984, in 1987 her & her family relocated to New Zealand  when she was 3 years old, I once read about her short biography segment on either the Drum/Tv guide magazines in June 2003 while @thetribeseries was running on Sabc-1, but i stand to be corrected at the same time.

# Diski General - Appreciation post to South African🇿🇦 -... | Facebook
## Diski General's Post
What a talent she is, incredible, memorable, She raised the South African  flag high up in the New Zealand  screens, she starred in shows such as Hercules, Shortland Street, Revelations: initial Journey (2003), the Legend seeker (2010) & other projects within NZ  television and theatre industries but mostly she will be remembered as Ebony on the New Zealand & British  Teenage Drama-Sci-fi Hit Series called @thetribeseries (1999-2003), one of the antagonist & protagonist characters of the show, she excelled on the show as Ebony , killed that Ebony part  one of the characters who appeared in every season of The-Tribe (1999-2003) by the way, not also forgetting her contributions on the drama's soundtrack album, opening theme song & also the lead singer of The-Tribe's Opening Theme song from Season 2 until Season 5.
I also learned that she also formed a musical band called Nubian Angels while she in her teens, with her older sisters in Megan & Monique (who were also part Of The-Tribe cast on Season 4 & 5).
She's around of course, a timeless talent, aging like fine wine, she looks like 18 years old , doing it in New Zealand  raising the  flags high up  .
This appreciation post is paying an ode to a South African  who excelled in the entertainment industry of New Zealand  with top perfection , For me as @thediskigeneral10 admin she's one of the greatest reasons why 18:30 on Sabc-1 in 2003 was a must watch, growing up In a East Rand township, giving me more hope & joy with her performance as Ebony on The Tribe series .
For me her acting skills remained me the legendary South African actresses such as the Great Daphney Hlomuka/Roseline Morapedi on the @thetribeseries
I used Stimela song instead of The Tribe songs to give a fitting South African  Flavour to Meryl
An ode to Ebony , We love You, No DNA, Just RSA .

And he said, “Read the play and tell me which character you think you need to play. I said, “Kivu, because she’s feisty and passionate and angry and I think I am all of those things.” He was like, “You’re none of those things. You are gonna play Naomi. She holds the stage in stillness and I think you don’t see yourself. But trust me.” We read it, and again I had this choice to make. I came to a fork in the road again. It was our final dress rehearsal for the play and I got a phone call that my uncle, who was like my father figure, everything to me, my best friend, had committed suicide. I was going to go on stage the next day and I remember thinking I’m really not meant to do this. Every time I act, something really terrible happens. I remember Menzi telling me, “Buddy, you don’t have to do this. I can do the role. I wrote it. I’ll be Naomi. I’ll change the name.” I just had this feeling that came over me, like this calmness, and I was just like, “I have to do it. I don’t know why, but I have to do it.” The funny thing about Naomi, her role was that she needed to connect the real world to the spiritual world and her role as an oracle was to guide the fallen people to their resting place. You cannot make it up. I remember doing that final dress rehearsal, and I got to a point and I could not stop crying, and the Playhouse Theatre people were watching and then Menzi explained to them afterwards and they were like, “We’ve never seen such resilience on the stage before. Never in all our years. Someone’s standing there, doing everything that they can, fighting on that stage for that moment.” Then it was opening night and at the end of it all I won a Durban Theater Award for Best Supporting Actress. I never ever felt like it was mine. It always feels like it is so out of reach, even if someone gives it to me. I always feel like I’m chasing it somehow. That’s what I mean about life, like it’s not me and it is, but every time I try to hide from it, it finds me. Even in this role, I me.
How did this role in _Prima Facie_ come about?

I was about to give up acting. Again. It’s like every second Tuesday. And then this brief lands in my email and I read it, and I felt like I had nothing left in me. I had done a role that traumatized me more than I thought it would, and I had to deal with what that meant for me. I kind of got a bit shattered by what it means to do something traumatic and have it played back to you and not realize what it meant in the moment. It’s hard. I think that’s why I don’t watch my own work. I think that’s why I kind of like theater, then I can leave and I don’t have to think about it being played back to me in some way. It feels more like it’s just for that moment and what happened in that moment is real and true and whatever it meant in that moment. The brief was there and again, I felt that feeling and I was like, “No, I can’t, I don’t have anything left.” I was shooting something in Cape Town. I go back to Joburg, I learn the lines and it was like I knew what the character was going to say next. I never perform anything for my husband, I just run lines with him and then I go in and audition, but this time, I actually just showed him and he burst into tears and he was like, “I think you’re meant to do it.” I get in to the audition room, I’m a screen actor- you go in, introduce yourself, you do the thing and they’re like, “We’ll be in touch,” and then they don’t. You can walk out there crying, and you gave your heart and soul in that audition room and no one cares. And [in this audition] they were like, come and sit down, tell us more about yourself. I thought that was the end of it. They’re just kind, lovely people. Then I got a callback and I saw who was on the callback list and I was like, “Well, I’m definitely not getting this.” I just thought to myself, there is no way. So I just went in there and I was like for the moment, I am gonna live in the truth of what the story means for me. There is nothing at stake here. Just the truth to live in this moment for one last time and leave it there and move on. And it feels cathartic.

Then they called me and told me that I got it and I was like, “You’re lying.” I sat in that for a while and now I’m doing it.
_Photo credit: Candice van Litsenborgh_
It was just such a profound experience to watch you in this role. I think the question I have for you, that Im sure everybody has, is how do you do this every night and twice on Saturday? I heard your process to get ready for a show is intense, but how are you doing this? And how are you taking care of yourself as a person?

I have got the best, most incredible people around me. So that helps. I’ve got friends who just come in and will be like, “Let me make you some tea and we’re gonna talk about things that have nothing to do with anything.” But I think what I’ve been realizing, about how I’ve been called to do this work, for me specifically, in every single job that has called me, I have had to hold my personal trauma and personal experience alongside very parallel to a character who has to hold it quite differently to the way that I hold it. And it unlocks things in me that I never knew I had. I’ve always been fit. I’ve always tried to [stay fit] because I got called into Action. I was never an Action actor. I’m actually very clumsy and I’m neurotic. I overthink everything and in Action you cannot overthink anything. You have to just be so solid in your conviction of everything. Action called me and I was like, “This feels like a bad joke.” I think boxing helped my diaphragm because of the breathing. That really helped. There’d be times I’m like, “I can’t breathe anymore.” And my husband was like, “It’s like good, because you’re not going to be able to breathe on stage. Find your breath, find your calm, keep moving, keep going. You’ve got this. You’ve got a warrior’s spirit. You have to fight for every moment on that stage.” I think that’s what it is. I’m a fighter. I didn’t know I was, but naturally I am. I fight for every breath and every moment on that stage. The preparation… I was grateful, I actually got a hip injury so I couldn’t walk for like 2 months before the show. When people say high stakes performance and everyone’s always been like, “Danica, you can do hard things.” And I was like, “Does it always have to be hard though?” A RomCom would be kind of cute. But I realized for that moment, my body needed to relax and I needed to sit with the script and kind of do the healing with what that meant for me, for that time. My body was telling me to stop moving. You need to be still with the script and really decide how you’re going to move with it and hold it. The body is an amazing thing I believe it is.

And they were like, “We’ve never seen an actor just like decide to run off and then come back on and be like no, I’m finishing the show.” It was insane. The psychology is: I want to run away. And then you have to constantly meet it every day and say, I am choosing because I am assigned to tell the story. Someone needs to hear this story. It’s bigger than me. And I know once I say “Thoroughbreds”, I’m safe.
_Photo credit: Candice van Litsenborgh_
It’s such an extraordinary feat and over two hours long. Ive read that the Broadway and West End productions were about 90 minutes, so what has been changed? I know that it has been localized as well.

Jodie Comer’s one is one hour, forty minutes. But what she does is, the lights don’t go down. She just goes. She literally goes from “Thoroughbreds. Today I was a winner. Today I came first.” It’s like a beat and then she goes into the next monologue and into the next. So there’s no breath, no process, no music in that moment. She’s moving everything around in process and just hammering it through. Whereas Neil was like, the audience needs to process. You need a moment to just move things, go back, step into the next moment. Every moment deserves its moment. That’s what I think has made it longer. We’re not going in one after the next. I think that’s what it is, but we didn’t change much at all, except for localizing it a bit, removing the jury. I think there’s one line that we had to cut out because there’s no jury in South Africa but everything has pretty much being kept the same to the point where I think people even said, “But you wouldn’t sit in a witness room. When you go to court, you’re sitting on a plastic chair waiting to go in and no one cares.” There was a lot that we wanted to change, but even then, they had to write an email really asking [Suzie Miller] if we could. I think we’re the only country in the world that has been given the right to localize it and change specific things, because everyone has done it in different languages, but they’ve done it in the context of the play. So even in China, they perform it as if it’s Liverpool or whatever, but in Chinese. They do it in their language but they haven’t changed the play and we’ve changed where its set. We tried to give it a piece of everything, she goes to UCT, so then Cape Town feels involved but then she’s now moved to Joburg, which is my story. I’m from KZN but I live in Joburg. And then with the accent, you find like a lot of people from KZN recognising it. I think I get some confused looks from some Capetonians, but then they finally get into it and feel who she is. It’s almost like I’m representing a piece of everyone a little bit, which is what we kind of wanted to do.

It is a long show, but I do think it’s because we’ve taken moments to let the audience breathe.
I saw it on opening night and learned that it was going to be two hours long. Neil Coppen actually walked past us and said, “People are going on and on like it’s The Odyssey.” But I think we need to remind ourselves that seeing something like this is almost like a feat of athleticism on stage. To see something like this, and the way that you held us for that duration, is extraordinary, and it’s not something that happens all the time. I remember walking out of the show saying, we are very lucky with what we just witnessed. It blew me away. You blew me away. And it’s worth mentioning, in the context of the show, that we are currently three women sitting here right now and in the show you talk about the statistic of 1 in 3 women.

I’m emotional today. I have never gotten my flowers in anything, and I got so many flowers on opening night. I just sat in my bedroom and cried because I feel like I’ve done works that are overlooked. And that’s how it is sometimes, and you just keep moving and you keep your head down. But then I realised that when people pay too much attention to me, that makes me uncomfortable as well. So I’m like, “What is it that I’m searching for?” And I’ve had to have this chat with myself and it’s the purpose and the assignment to story like, what does it mean? I’ve had people come up to me and tell me, “You’re telling my story. It was mine,” and I look at them in that moment and I feel so strong in that moment. But when I go home I’m just me. Tessa is the strong one. Tessa is the one that everyone is looking at and thinking, “Wow she’s so strong.” I go home to me, and I sit with that and I think, “Can I do it again?” Every day I ask myself that. I have never reconciled it in my mind that I’ll be able to do it again. My stage managers is like, “I’ve never met an actress like you, honestly.” I come in four hours before so I can walk the show by myself, with my words, and do every single movement, do everything and be like, “Okay now I have proof that I can do it. So I’ll do it.” I just want to prove once a day that I can do it and then I’ll do it at night.
_Photo credit: Candice van Litsenborgh_
Originally, when I used to run Sarafina Magazine, I never asked women about motherhood because I felt that men weren’t getting asked about fatherhood so I wasnt going to ask women that question. However, since my last interview back in 2020, I’ve had a little one of my own. And I feel like I can’t not ask about how it’s informed you as an artist, because for me, it was such a a big cellular shift. So that’s the reason that I want to ask: how do you feel motherhood has informed you as as an artist?

Wow. I feel like what it’s done is it’s given me something to grasp onto that is an embodiment of the nurturer and the warrior as one. It’s fleshed me out in ways that I never expected it to. I have an empathy and a sympathy for everything and everyone more than I think I would. I also feel, and I’ve been given this a lot, people often say I’m very giving. If I am holding other actors, even if I’m off camera, if my character cried on camera, I’m crying off camera, because you also need to respond to what that meant in that moment. I will stand in. People will be like, “I can do it to a tennis ball. It’s fine.” And I’m like, “But I’m here.” I think it’s that thing of being able to hold so much. It fleshes you out in ways where you realize that things are bigger than you, and also, that they are a part of you in so many different ways. It also makes me think of every single person as being an extension of me, so be it to say. But it does feel that way because I look at my son, he’s 15 now. I look at him, I had him when I was 21. I look at him and he’s this man. And even in this play, I wonder what that means. I ask him often, “Do you know what it means? Do you know what it means to be a man? Do you know what it means for a woman to experience you? What do you know?” He watched something that I was in where my character got hurt a lot, but he loves Action and his visceral responds to that was heartbreaking because in the beginning he was like, “Go, mom, Kick ass!” And then he got to a point where my husband said he just shrunk a bit. Because as everyone sees you as “Jessica Brok,” he sees his mom. So, I was like, “Okay, he’ll watch the Jodie Comer version and he won’t watch this version.” Simply because my mum even said it was so painful to watch because it was like, “It’s Tessa, no it’s Danica, no, it’s Tessa.” And as people who know you and know your journey and your story, it’s hard. I think it’s informed that something is bigger than me. Something’s always bigger than than me.

I said, “Kivu, because she’s feisty and passionate and angry and I think I am all of those things.” He was like, “You’re none of those things. You are gonna play Naomi. She holds the stage in stillness and I think you don’t see yourself. But trust me.” We read it, and again I had this choice to make. I came to a fork in the road again. It was our final dress rehearsal for the play and I got a phone call that my uncle, who was like my father figure, everything to me, my best friend, had committed suicide. I was going to go on stage the next day and I remember thinking I’m really not meant to do this. Every time I act, something really terrible happens. I remember Menzi telling me, “Buddy, you don’t have to do this. I can do the role. I wrote it. I’ll be Naomi. I’ll change the name.” I just had this feeling that came over me, like this calmness, and I was just like, “I have to do it. I don’t know why, but I have to do it.” The funny thing about Naomi, her role was that she needed to connect the real world to the spiritual world and her role as an oracle was to guide the fallen people to their resting place. You cannot make it up. I remember doing that final dress rehearsal, and I got to a point and I could not stop crying, and the Playhouse Theatre people were watching and then Menzi explained to them afterwards and they were like, “We’ve never seen such resilience on the stage before. Never in all our years. Someone’s standing there, doing everything that they can, fighting on that stage for that moment.” Then it was opening night and at the end of it all I won a Durban Theater Award for Best Supporting Actress. I never ever felt like it was mine. It always feels like it is so out of reach, even if someone gives it to me. I always feel like I’m chasing it somehow. That’s what I mean about life, like it’s not me and it is, but every time I try to hide from it, it finds me. Even in this role, I me.
How did this role in _Prima Facie_ come about?
texts.4: I was about to give up acting. Again. It’s like every second Tuesday. And then this brief lands in my email and I read it, and I felt like I had nothing left in me. I had done a role that traumatized me more than I thought it would, and I had to deal with what that meant for me. I kind of got a bit shattered by what it means to do something traumatic and have it played back to you and not realize what it meant in the moment. It’s hard. I think that’s why I don’t watch my own work. I think that’s why I kind of like theater, then I can leave and I don’t have to think about it being played back to me in some way. It feels more like it’s just for that moment and what happened in that moment is real and true and whatever it meant in that moment. The brief was there and again, I felt that feeling and I was like, “No, I can’t, I don’t have anything left.” I was shooting something in Cape Town. I go back to Joburg, I learn the lines and it was like I knew what the character was going to say next. I never perform anything for my husband, I just run lines with him and then I go in and audition, but this time, I actually just showed him and he burst into tears and he was like, “I think you’re meant to do it.” I get in to the audition room, I’m a screen actor- you go in, introduce yourself, you do the thing and they’re like, “We’ll be in touch,” and then they don’t. You can walk out there crying, and you gave your heart and soul in that audition room and no one cares. And [in this audition] they were like, come and sit down, tell us more about yourself. I thought that was the end of it. They’re just kind, lovely people. Then I got a callback and I saw who was on the callback list and I was like, “Well, I’m definitely not getting this.” I just thought to myself, there is no way. So I just went in there and I was like for the moment, I am gonna live in the truth of what the story means for me. There is nothing at stake here. Just the truth to live in this moment for one last time and leave it there and move on. And it feels cathartic.

Then they called me and told me that I got it and I was like, “You’re lying.” I sat in that for a while and now I’m doing it.
_Photo credit: Candice van Litsenborgh_
It was just such a profound experience to watch you in this role. I think the question I have for you, that Im sure everybody has, is how do you do this every night and twice on Saturday? I heard your process to get ready for a show is intense, but how are you doing this? And how are you taking care of yourself as a person?

And it unlocks things in me that I never knew I had. I’ve always been fit. I’ve always tried to [stay fit] because I got called into Action. I was never an Action actor. There’d be times I’m like, “I can’t breathe anymore.” And my husband was like, “It’s like good, because you’re not going to be able to breathe on stage. I didn’t know I was, but naturally I am. I fight for every breath and every moment on that stage. The preparation… I was grateful, I actually got a hip injury so I couldn’t walk for like 2 months before the show. But I realized for that moment, my body needed to relax and I needed to sit with the script and kind of do the healing with what that meant for me, for that time. My body was telling me to stop moving. You need to be still with the script and really decide how you’re going to move with it and hold it. The body is an amazing thing I believe it is.

opened.information:
Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva
Title: Oksana Grigorieva
Chunks: 4,5,6,7
Grigorieva gained attention as a songwriter in 2006, after the song that she wrote, "Un día llegará" (Translated from Spanish: A Day Will Come), became popular on the Josh Groban album, _Awake_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTESerpe2010-3)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZeidler2009-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-wennfact-7)_Las Vegas Review-Journal_ highlighted "Un día llegará" in particular in a review of Groban's album _Awake_, commenting, "Groban's most effective tunes tend to be his most unadorned, when he favors understatement over ostentation, such as on the flickering piano ballad 'Lullaby' or the tremulous slow burn of 'Un día llegará,' with its touches of flamenco guitar."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-bracelin-8) Prior to singing "Un día llegará" at a 2007 live performance, the song was "endorsed as a beauty" by Groban, in a statement to his fans.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-bialczak-9) In a review of _Awake_, the _Philippine Daily Inquirer_ called "Un día llegará" an "outstanding track".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-asilo-10) Fred Shuster of _Los Angeles Daily News_ reviewed the album, and commented, "The gorgeous 'Un día llegará,' opening with a sweep of guitar, sets the mood for romantic highlights to come".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-shuster-11)

In 2009, Grigorieva's music album _Beautiful Heartache_ was released; Mel Gibson supplementing her music career at the time by serving as executive producer.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMachell2009-2) The album includes 11 tracks, and features a cover of the Russian song "Dark Eyes" and a collaboration with Charlie Midnight.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-johnlauren-12)_Beautiful Heartache_ was marketed as "grown-up, piano-led pop, heavy on classical motifs".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMachell2009-2) Save for the song "Say My Name", which was co-written with Gibson, Grigorieva wrote the entire album on her own. "Say My Name" was included in the 2010 film _Edge of Darkness_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-metrolover-13)_ABC News_ reported that _Beautiful Heartache_ garnered the singer "rave reviews" from music critics.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-breaksonto-14)_Reuters_ commented of the album, "'Beautiful Heartache' features a collection of wistful love songs, blending shimmering string arrangements with pop and jazz-influenced arrangements that showcase Grigorieva's soulful voice."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZeidler2009-6) In a review of the album, Jack Foley of _IndieLondon_ gave it a rating of 4 out of 5, and observed, "throughout, she displays a keen ear for melody, for honest emotional simplicity and classic values. She’s well worth taking the time to check out".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-foley-15)

In December 2012 it was revealed Grigorieva was taking a detour into hip hop and dance music, scheduled for release in 2013.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-16)
Grigorieva was married in 1989 for three months to Russian lawyer Igor Baranov.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-17) In 1992, she married British artist Nicholas Rowland.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTESerpe2010-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-ognews-5) She had a relationship with James Bond actor Timothy Dalton;[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTERiggs2007-18) Grigorieva met Dalton in 1995 while she was employed as a translator for filmmaker Nikita Mikhalkov.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTESerpe2010-3) Dalton and Grigorieva had a son together (born August 1997) named Alexander. Their relationship ended in 2003.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTERiggs2007-18)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMachell2009-2)
Grigorieva has been involved in charity work with Chernobyl Children's Project International in Belarus.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-19)

### Relationship and breakup with Mel Gibson
[edit]
Starting in 2007, Grigorieva was romantically involved with actor Mel Gibson,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-messier-20) and their daughter Lucia was born on 30 October 2009.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-dinunno-21) The couple separated in April 2010.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-leonard-22) In June 2010, Grigorieva obtained a restraining order against Gibson, after stating he had physically assaulted her.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-restrainingorders-23) Gibson was barred from coming near Grigorieva or their daughter.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-guardianjuly2-24) In July 2010, Gibson was identified as a possible suspect in a domestic violence investigation initiated after detectives spoke in Malibu to Grigorieva.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCartney2010-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVancouver_Sun2010-26) Grigorieva and Gibson were involved in a child custody dispute involving their daughter in a confidential court case.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCartney2010-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVancouver_Sun2010-26)

texts.4: Grigorieva gained attention as a songwriter in 2006, after the song that she wrote, "Un día llegará" (Translated from Spanish: A Day Will Come), became popular on the Josh Groban album, _Awake_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTESerpe2010-3)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZeidler2009-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-wennfact-7)_Las Vegas Review-Journal_ highlighted "Un día llegará" in particular in a review of Groban's album _Awake_, commenting, "Groban's most effective tunes tend to be his most unadorned, when he favors understatement over ostentation, such as on the flickering piano ballad 'Lullaby' or the tremulous slow burn of 'Un día llegará,' with its touches of flamenco guitar."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-bracelin-8) Prior to singing "Un día llegará" at a 2007 live performance, the song was "endorsed as a beauty" by Groban, in a statement to his fans.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-bialczak-9) In a review of _Awake_, the _Philippine Daily Inquirer_ called "Un día llegará" an "outstanding track".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-asilo-10) Fred Shuster of _Los Angeles Daily News_ reviewed the album, and commented, "The gorgeous 'Un día llegará,' opening with a sweep of guitar, sets the mood for romantic highlights to come".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-shuster-11)
texts.5: In 2009, Grigorieva's music album _Beautiful Heartache_ was released; Mel Gibson supplementing her music career at the time by serving as executive producer.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMachell2009-2) The album includes 11 tracks, and features a cover of the Russian song "Dark Eyes" and a collaboration with Charlie Midnight.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-johnlauren-12)_Beautiful Heartache_ was marketed as "grown-up, piano-led pop, heavy on classical motifs".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMachell2009-2) Save for the song "Say My Name", which was co-written with Gibson, Grigorieva wrote the entire album on her own. "Say My Name" was included in the 2010 film _Edge of Darkness_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-metrolover-13)_ABC News_ reported that _Beautiful Heartache_ garnered the singer "rave reviews" from music critics.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-breaksonto-14)_Reuters_ commented of the album, "'Beautiful Heartache' features a collection of wistful love songs, blending shimmering string arrangements with pop and jazz-influenced arrangements that showcase Grigorieva's soulful voice."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZeidler2009-6) In a review of the album, Jack Foley of _IndieLondon_ gave it a rating of 4 out of 5, and observed, "throughout, she displays a keen ear for melody, for honest emotional simplicity and classic values. She’s well worth taking the time to check out".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-foley-15)
texts.6:
In December 2012 it was revealed Grigorieva was taking a detour into hip hop and dance music, scheduled for release in 2013.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-16)
Grigorieva was married in 1989 for three months to Russian lawyer Igor Baranov.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-17) In 1992, she married British artist Nicholas Rowland.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTESerpe2010-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-ognews-5) She had a relationship with James Bond actor Timothy Dalton;[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTERiggs2007-18) Grigorieva met Dalton in 1995 while she was employed as a translator for filmmaker Nikita Mikhalkov.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTESerpe2010-3) Dalton and Grigorieva had a son together (born August 1997) named Alexander. Their relationship ended in 2003.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTERiggs2007-18)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMachell2009-2)
Grigorieva has been involved in charity work with Chernobyl Children's Project International in Belarus.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-19)
texts.7:
### Relationship and breakup with Mel Gibson
[edit]
Starting in 2007, Grigorieva was romantically involved with actor Mel Gibson,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-messier-20) and their daughter Lucia was born on 30 October 2009.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-dinunno-21) The couple separated in April 2010.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-leonard-22) In June 2010, Grigorieva obtained a restraining order against Gibson, after stating he had physically assaulted her.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-restrainingorders-23) Gibson was barred from coming near Grigorieva or their daughter.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-guardianjuly2-24) In July 2010, Gibson was identified as a possible suspect in a domestic violence investigation initiated after detectives spoke in Malibu to Grigorieva.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCartney2010-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVancouver_Sun2010-26) Grigorieva and Gibson were involved in a child custody dispute involving their daughter in a confidential court case.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCartney2010-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oksana_Grigorieva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVancouver_Sun2010-26)

# Jimmy Kimmel live | There was no apartment waiting in New York, no record company left to call, and a baby still needed to be fed | Facebook
### **There was no apartment waiting in New York, no record company left to call, and a baby still needed to be fed.**
Emmylou Harris had gone to Greenwich Village believing music might give her a life there. She married songwriter Tom Slocum, recorded her first album, *Gliding Bird*, and became a mother at twenty-two. Then almost everything holding that new life together gave way at once. The album failed, the label collapsed, and the marriage ended within about a year. With her infant daughter Hallie, Emmylou went back to her parents in Maryland.
She later remembered that return without romance. She was broke, on food stamps, and unsure whether she had misjudged the future completely. Her parents did not ask her to explain herself. Their house simply became available again.
Emmylou began singing around Washington, D.C., putting together a small folk trio and taking local work where she could find it. Her parents helped with Hallie, making it possible for her to leave the house for rehearsals and evening performances without pretending she no longer had a child depending on her. Years later, Emmylou said that arrangement was the reason she could keep going.
The house gradually became part of the working life too. Band members came through. Her parents knew the musicians, hosted barbecues and front-yard football games, and absorbed the odd hours that followed a daughter whose career was slowly becoming less local. What had started as a retreat from a failed beginning became the safest place from which she could try again.
Not long afterward, Gram Parsons heard Emmylou sing and asked her to work with him, beginning the partnership that redirected her toward country music. That chapter would become the one history remembered. The quieter one came just before it, when there was still no guarantee of anything. A young mother had gone home because she had nowhere else to go, and a pair of parents made enough room in an ordinary house for both a granddaughter and a second attempt at a life in music.

# These Huge Stars Quit Hollywood And Started Totally Different Lives
## 1.Cameron Diaz
Elisabetta Villa / Getty Images
**Who she was in Hollywood:** For two decades following her debut in 1994's hit _The Mask_, Cameron remained one of Hollywood's biggest stars, equally adept at comedies (like _There's Something About Mary_) and dramas (like _Vanilla Sky_). She was also one of Charlie's Angels and the voice of Fiona in _Shrek_!
**Why she left:** Cameron last appeared onscreen in 2014's _Annie_. In 2018 she announced she was retired, later saying, "I don't miss performing," and that she really enjoyed having time for herself. She also recently became a mother, welcoming a daughter, Raddix, in December.

# These Huge Stars Quit Hollywood And Started Totally Different Lives
## 2.Rick Moranis
Disney
**Who he was in Hollywood:** Rick was a major comedy star in the '80s, starting out on the Canadian comedy sketch show _SCTV_ and then starring in movies (often alongside Steve Martin) like _Ghostbusters_, _Spaceballs_, _Parenthood_, _The Flintstones_, and the _Honey, I Shrunk the Kids_ franchise.
**Why he left:** Sadly, Rick’s wife, Ann, died of cancer in 1991 at the age of 35, leaving Rick a single parent to their two young children. So after filming 1997’s _Honey, We Shrunk Ourselves_, Rick left Hollywood to focus on raising his kids full time. He hasn’t appeared on the big screen since (though he has done the occasional voice role). His 23-year-old hiatus may come to an end soon, though: There are plans for him to star in a new _Honey, I Shrunk the Kids_ film called _Shrunk_, with Josh Gad playing his son.

# These Huge Stars Quit Hollywood And Started Totally Different Lives
## 3.Phoebe Cates
Universal, Angela Weiss / Getty Images
**Who she was in Hollywood:** Phoebe was just about everyone's crush in the '80s, thanks to her iconic performance in _Fast Times at Ridgemont High_. She later starred in the _Gremlins_ films, which were worldwide smashes.
**Why she left:** In 1989, Phoebe married actor Kevin Kline, and the couple went on to have two children, Greta (who records music under the name Frankie Cosmos) and Owen. Kline told Playboy magazine that the couple "agreed to alternate so that we're never working at the same time … [but] whenever it's been her slot to work, Phoebe has chosen to stay with the children." Phoebe's last starring role was in 1994's _Princess Caraboo_, although she made a small appearance in 2001's _The Anniversary Party_ as a favor to Jennifer Jason Leigh, her friend and _Fast Times_ costar. Phoebe also owns and operates the Blue Tree boutique in New York City.

# Jimmy Kimmel live | There was no apartment waiting in New York, no record company left to call, and a baby still needed to be fed | Facebook
### **There was no apartment waiting in New York, no record company left to call, and a baby still needed to be fed.**
Emmylou Harris had gone to Greenwich Village believing music might give her a life there. She married songwriter Tom Slocum, recorded her first album, *Gliding Bird*, and became a mother at twenty-two. Then almost everything holding that new life together gave way at once. The album failed, the label collapsed, and the marriage ended within about a year. With her infant daughter Hallie, Emmylou went back to her parents in Maryland.
She later remembered that return without romance. She was broke, on food stamps, and unsure whether she had misjudged the future completely. Her parents did not ask her to explain herself. Their house simply became available again.
Emmylou began singing around Washington, D.C., putting together a small folk trio and taking local work where she could find it. Her parents helped with Hallie, making it possible for her to leave the house for rehearsals and evening performances without pretending she no longer had a child depending on her. Years later, Emmylou said that arrangement was the reason she could keep going.
The house gradually became part of the working life too. Band members came through. Her parents knew the musicians, hosted barbecues and front-yard football games, and absorbed the odd hours that followed a daughter whose career was slowly becoming less local. What had started as a retreat from a failed beginning became the safest place from which she could try again.
Not long afterward, Gram Parsons heard Emmylou sing and asked her to work with him, beginning the partnership that redirected her toward country music. That chapter would become the one history remembered. The quieter one came just before it, when there was still no guarantee of anything. A young mother had gone home because she had nowhere else to go, and a pair of parents made enough room in an ordinary house for both a granddaughter and a second attempt at a life in music.

# These Huge Stars Quit Hollywood And Started Totally Different Lives
## 1.Cameron Diaz
Elisabetta Villa / Getty Images
**Who she was in Hollywood:** For two decades following her debut in 1994's hit _The Mask_, Cameron remained one of Hollywood's biggest stars, equally adept at comedies (like _There's Something About Mary_) and dramas (like _Vanilla Sky_). She was also one of Charlie's Angels and the voice of Fiona in _Shrek_!
**Why she left:** Cameron last appeared onscreen in 2014's _Annie_. In 2018 she announced she was retired, later saying, "I don't miss performing," and that she really enjoyed having time for herself. She also recently became a mother, welcoming a daughter, Raddix, in December.

# These Huge Stars Quit Hollywood And Started Totally Different Lives
## 2.Rick Moranis
Disney
**Who he was in Hollywood:** Rick was a major comedy star in the '80s, starting out on the Canadian comedy sketch show _SCTV_ and then starring in movies (often alongside Steve Martin) like _Ghostbusters_, _Spaceballs_, _Parenthood_, _The Flintstones_, and the _Honey, I Shrunk the Kids_ franchise.
**Why he left:** Sadly, Rick’s wife, Ann, died of cancer in 1991 at the age of 35, leaving Rick a single parent to their two young children. So after filming 1997’s _Honey, We Shrunk Ourselves_, Rick left Hollywood to focus on raising his kids full time. He hasn’t appeared on the big screen since (though he has done the occasional voice role). His 23-year-old hiatus may come to an end soon, though: There are plans for him to star in a new _Honey, I Shrunk the Kids_ film called _Shrunk_, with Josh Gad playing his son.

# These Huge Stars Quit Hollywood And Started Totally Different Lives
## 3.Phoebe Cates
Universal, Angela Weiss / Getty Images
**Who she was in Hollywood:** Phoebe was just about everyone's crush in the '80s, thanks to her iconic performance in _Fast Times at Ridgemont High_. She later starred in the _Gremlins_ films, which were worldwide smashes.
**Why she left:** In 1989, Phoebe married actor Kevin Kline, and the couple went on to have two children, Greta (who records music under the name Frankie Cosmos) and Owen. Kline told Playboy magazine that the couple "agreed to alternate so that we're never working at the same time … [but] whenever it's been her slot to work, Phoebe has chosen to stay with the children." Phoebe's last starring role was in 1994's _Princess Caraboo_, although she made a small appearance in 2001's _The Anniversary Party_ as a favor to Jennifer Jason Leigh, her friend and _Fast Times_ costar. Phoebe also owns and operates the Blue Tree boutique in New York City.
